title: Sablés Diamants (French Butter Cookies)
summary: Crisp, buttery French sablés sliced from a chilled log and rolled in coarse sugar for a sparkling, crunchy edge - a simple make-ahead biscuit with a short, sandy crumb.
equipment: 2 large metal baking trays lined with baking paper
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cream the base
steps.text: Beat the softened butter, icing sugar and salt on low-medium speed for just 1 minute, until smooth and creamy rather than light and fluffy. Keeping the mixing brief limits the air you beat in, which is what gives these biscuits their sandy, melt-in-the-mouth texture rather than a cakey one.

steps.title: Add yolk and vanilla
steps.text: Beat in the egg yolk and vanilla extract until fully combined and glossy. The yolk adds richness and a little structure without introducing the extra water a whole egg would bring, which keeps the dough short.

steps.title: Bring in the flour
steps.text: Add the plain flour on low speed and mix only until the dough just comes together. Overworking at this stage develops gluten and makes the biscuits tough, so stop as soon as no dry flour remains visible.

steps.title: Shape and chill the logs
steps.text: Divide the dough in two and roll each half into a log about 4cm thick on a lightly floured surface, then wrap tightly. Chill for at least 3 hours, or freeze for 1 hour, until very firm; a properly firm log slices cleanly into neat rounds instead of squashing out of shape.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) at least 20 minutes before baking, so it reaches a steady temperature by the time the biscuits go in. An oven that hasn't fully come up to heat bakes unevenly and can leave the biscuits pale and soft.

steps.title: Coat in sugar
steps.text: Brush the chilled logs all over with the lightly beaten egg white, then roll them in the demerara or coarse sugar, pressing gently so it sticks. This sugary coating is what gives sablés diamants their name, catching the light like tiny diamonds once baked.

steps.title: Slice and space out
steps.text: Slice the logs into rounds about 1cm thick and arrange them 3cm apart on the lined trays, as they will spread slightly as they bake. Even spacing stops the edges from baking into one another.

steps.title: Bake until sandy-pale
steps.text: Bake one tray at a time for 14-17 minutes, until the edges turn golden but the tops stay pale and sandy-looking. Baking only the edges to colour keeps the crumb short and prevents the biscuits from drying out in the centre.

steps.title: Cool and set
steps.text: Leave the biscuits on the tray for 5 minutes to firm up, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely. They continue to crisp as they cool, so resist stacking them while still warm.

tips: Keep the butter at around 18°C - too soft and the dough will be sticky to roll, too cold and it won't cream evenly.
A common mistake is overbeating the butter and sugar until pale and fluffy; mix briefly instead so the biscuits stay short and sandy rather than turning cakey.
If the logs soften while you're coating them in sugar, pop them back in the fridge for 10 minutes before slicing - cold dough gives much neater rounds.
Bake one tray at a time in the centre of the oven so every biscuit browns evenly.
Let the biscuits cool fully before storing, as they firm up and become crisp only once completely cold.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 5 days. The unbaked dough logs can be frozen, well wrapped, for up to 2 months - slice and bake from frozen, adding a minute or two to the baking time.
